channel.title: Pocallum — Barcelona
channel.description: Cultural photography. Jazz, blues, theatre, dance and performing arts. Barcelona.

item.title: Festival de Blues de Barcelona
item.description:
The Blues de Barcelona is a different species. The loyalty of its audience, the calibre of musicians who pass through, the care taken with every edition — nothing here is superficial or accidental.

Photographing blues is photographing scars. Every musician carries a story you can see in their hands, their posture, the way they lean into the microphone as if they have something important to tell it.

Not everyone understands the blues at first glance. But everyone understands a photograph that genuinely captures it.

item.title: Jornades Xarxa 9 Barris Acull
item.description:
For almost two decades, 9 Barris Acull was the district’s welcome centre: legal advice on immigration, language workshops, a neighbourhood solidarity network — and every year, a series of talks that put on the table the questions the rest of the city preferred not to face.

Each edition had its theme. In 2017, different perspectives on Islam and racism. In 2018, discriminatory discourse and its alternatives. In 2019, the new demographic landscape and the challenges of coexistence. In 2022, young people, racism and exclusion. These were not consensus events — they were sessions of intellectual confrontation, with people who lived these issues first-hand.

item.title: Jazz I Am
item.description:
Jazz I Am is the festival that changes format every year. New venues, new proposals, emerging names alongside established references. Barcelona jazz in a moment of permanent redefinition.

We’ve followed Jazz I Am since the early editions, and every year is different from the last. That’s one of the things we love most: you never quite know where you’re headed or what you’ll find.

Unexpected venues. Groups you’d never heard of. A set that runs long because nobody wants it to end.

item.title: ESMUC End-of-Year Concerts
item.description:
Every spring, the Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya closes the academic year with a series of concerts where students perform under professional conditions. We documented the 2023–2024 edition on film: Leica M6, Summicron 50mm and APX400 pushed to 3200.

ESMUC trains musicians in jazz, classical, traditional and modern music. The end-of-year concerts are not an academic showcase — they are real concerts, played by musicians who are about to step into the professional world.

item.title: Festival de Sopes del Món
item.description:
Every autumn, Nou Barris fills with pots. The Festival de Sopes del Món — Festival of World Soups — proves that a simple bowl of soup can bring people together in ways no politics can manage. Organised by 9 Barris Acull and the Xarxa d’Intercanvi de Coneixements, it has now reached its nineteenth edition.

The festival brings together communities from across the neighbourhood — and the world — around a bowl of soup. Each participant brings their recipe, their story and their table. The result is a gathering that is as much political as gastronomic, in the best sense of both words.

item.title: La Juganera is now in our festivals section — and we were there last Friday
item.description: We covered the sixth edition of La Juganera at Nau Bostik. A neighbourhood festival that grows a little each year without losing what it is.

item.title: Nou Barris meets New Orleans
item.description:
Every spring, the Ateneu Popular 9 Barris builds an imaginary bridge between Nou Barris and New Orleans. Not a tourist postcard — a recognition that both cities share something fundamental: music as a tool for social cohesion in neighbourhoods that need it.

The formula is simple and effective: a second line through the district streets, a brass band that brings people out onto their balconies, DJ sets with a soundsystem, Creole food, and a closing concert. All in one day, for everyone.

item.title: La Juganera
item.description:
La Juganera is not a festival built around a line-up. It is a neighbourhood festival, organised by the community itself, that takes place at Nau Bostik and grows a little each year without losing what makes it what it is: the programme is chosen by the festival committee, and the festival committee is everyone.

We have covered La Juganera since its third edition. Each year the programme mixes percussion, street bands, DJs and music that doesn’t fit a single label. What never changes is the atmosphere: participatory, with no distance between musicians and audience, and the people of Nou Barris as the main protagonists.

item.title: Jazz I Am 2026 — When a small festival has more to say than a big one
item.description: Full photographic coverage of the eighth edition of the showcase organised by Taller de Músics at El Molino, Barcelona.

item.title: Chinese New Year in Barcelona
item.description:
Barcelona’s Chinese community celebrates the lunar new year with dragons, fire, music and food. It is not a spectacle designed for tourists — it is a tradition brought to the street because the street belongs to everyone. A welcoming and extraordinary celebration that keeps growing year after year. Since 2017, we have been there whenever we can.

The celebrations don’t always happen in the same place or on the same date. Sometimes it’s at Parc de l’Estació del Nord. Other times in the city centre, around the Arc de Triomf. The display put on by residents of Chinese origin is extraordinary — both in central Barcelona and in the neighbourhoods where they have built roots. In 2026, across two days, we documented two editions: the central Barcelona celebration and the Nou Barris one, where the community organises its own event along Via Júlia down to Plaça Ángel Pestaña.

item.title: Carnestoltes in Nou Barris
item.description:
Nou Barris celebrates Carnestoltes in the street — and it does it properly. The Gran Rua Central winds through the district with comparses, costumes and batucadas. Those who want to keep going head to Ateneu Popular de Nou Barris, where the Gran Ball de Carnestoltes runs until the night runs out.

We have been documenting Nou Barris Carnestoltes since 2016. Two distinct moments: the daytime parade, with February light and families in the street, and the Ateneu party, where the energy is something else entirely. Artificial light, movement, costumes that looked one way in the sun and look completely different on the dance floor.

item.title: Sax-o-Rama
item.description:
Sax-o-Rama is the international saxophone festival created by Dani Nel·lo — a reference point in its field that brings saxophonists from across the world to La Paloma year after year.

La Paloma has its own character, and Sax-o-Rama makes the most of it: concerts mixing musicians from Japan, the Caribbean and across Spain alongside the Barcelona Big Blues Band as the connecting thread. Every edition is different, but the saxophone is always at the centre.

item.title: Ciutat Flamenco Barcelona
item.description:
A spectacular festival where dance is almost more of a protagonist than flamenco itself. A brilliant initiative from Taller de Músics.

Ciutat Flamenco is the Barcelona festival that treats flamenco as what it is: a living art, in permanent evolution, capable of absorbing contemporary dance, audiovisual research and interdisciplinary collaboration without losing its roots.

It started at Nau Bostik, when I photographed the presentation of Vanesa Aibar and the Estampa collective’s Cristalización IV. There I ran into programmer Lluís Cabrera, whom I already knew from Flamenco de Barrio, and with the organisation’s permission I was able to cover the rest of the festival.

item.title: Flamenco de Barrio
item.description:
Flamenco de Barrio takes flamenco to the street. Literally. Squares, courtyards, everyday spaces in Nou Barris where something that shouldn’t fit suddenly fits perfectly.

Some festivals bring the audience to the artists. Flamenco de Barrio does the opposite: it brings the artists to the people who are already there.

Photographing in natural afternoon light, in spaces not designed for performance, with the audience so close they become part of the image — this is a different school. Here we’ve learnt that the best photograph isn’t always the perfect one.

item.title: Sopar d'Entitats del Casal de Barri Prosperitat
item.description:
Every autumn, the organisations and collectives of the neighbourhood gather at Casal de Barri Prosperitat to take stock, welcome new members and reconnect with those no longer as active. The Sopar d’Entitats (Organisations’ Dinner) is an annual tradition mixing debate, food, music and comedy — almost a festival, even if it doesn’t go by that name.

We play at home here. La Prosperitat is our neighbourhood, the Casal is our space, and the organisations that come — we know them. There is a warmth and a horizontality to this dinner that no conventional festival can replicate: nobody is the audience, everyone is a participant.

item.title: Clot amb Blues
item.description:
Among the finest festivals there are. All soul and small format. Proximity with the performers, with the organisation, and everything made with great care and love.

El Clot is a neighbourhood that has made blues its own. Clot amb Blues brings the music to the neighbourhood’s own spaces — squares, venues, local facilities — with the intention of making music something that belongs to residents, not just to audiences.

Small in scale, large in content. Live concerts, street processions, proposals that go beyond the standard concert. The festival understands that neighbourhood music is, by definition, the kind that takes root deepest.

item.title: Circus Show — International Exchange
item.description:
The Circus School of the Ateneu Popular de 9 Barris has spent years training young people from the district in circus disciplines. The Mostra de Circ is the moment when everything they have learned comes out into the street — literally. An open space, in the middle of the square, with the neighbourhood as audience and the students as protagonists.

Circus is very present in Nou Barris. And it is no coincidence: it is a tool for social transformation that the district has understood and supported for decades. The Ateneu Popular de 9 Barris is its centre of gravity — but circus appears in the neighbourhood centres, the squares, youth festivals, international exchanges.

item.title: Pícnic de Blues
item.description:
Every May, Capibola Blues brings blues music to Parc Central de Nou Barris as part of the district’s neighbourhood festivities. A blanket on the grass, a cool box, live music and spring sunshine — or rain, which has also happened. Since 2013, we have been there.

The Pícnic de Blues is a free, neighbourhood event with no pretensions, which for some reason always works. Perhaps because blues in a park, with people lying on the grass and kids running through the crowd, is exactly the right setting for this music.

item.title: Barcelona Tattoo Expo · BAUM
item.description:
The Barcelona Tattoo Expo has been, for more than two decades, the most important tattoo art festival in southern Europe. We have been there from the beginning — as the organisation’s official photographers, edition after edition.

Tattooing is an art you live on your skin, in every sense. Photographing it means entering a world of masters, schools, traditions that travel across continents and converge in Barcelona’s exhibition halls three days a year.

item.title: Ventanas Abiertas — Finestres Curioses
item.description:
Ventanas Abiertas / Finestres Curioses is a community artistic creation process: a performance built from the contributions of the people who live in the neighbourhood, not from a script written by someone from outside. The result is a show that carries the imprint of Nou Barris in every movement.

It is facilitated by Elia Pérez and Marta Rodríguez at the Ateneu Popular de Nou Barris. The process matters as much as the premiere: weeks of collective work in which participants — residents of all ages — build a performance from scratch. Circus disciplines appear as an expressive language, not as technical virtuosity.
